subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
subcategory: Privacy Laws That Changed the World
title: India's Digital Personal Data Protection
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on India's Digital Personal Data Protection.

hook.text: India has 1.4 billion people and the world's largest biometric database. It just got its first privacy law.

buildup.text: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, passed in 2023, establishes consent and purpose limitation.

discovery.text: The law gives citizens the right to correction, erasure, and grievance redress for data misuse.

twist.text: Critics say the law gives the government broad exemptions for national security — a loophole for state surveillance.

climax.text: India's law protects citizens from corporations but may not protect them from their own government.

punchline.text: Privacy from companies. But not from the state.

quiz.question: What is the main criticism of India's data protection law?
options: Broad government exemptions for national security create a surveillance loophole
It's too strict for businesses to comply with
It doesn't cover digital data at all
